html: The Nhuwala are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, in the coastal country west of the Robe River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Little is recorded about them. Their neighbours were the Thalanyji to the southwest, the Martuthunira to the northeast and the Kurrama and Pinikura inland. Sheep stations took up this coast from the late 1800s.
